% Retained-title-surface probe for the v3 generic-API contraction (issue #84).
%
% The defensible small-caps behavior used by lanepaper's retained front matter
% must stay available but PRIVATE (\lnp@titlesc), with no public alias, and the
% title surface must still render.
%
% RED before #84 (\lnp@titlesc absent, public \titlesc present); GREEN after.
\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage{lanepaper}

\makeatletter
% Retained front-matter small caps is present and private.
\@ifundefined{lnp@titlesc}%
  {\PackageError{title}{Private front-matter small caps lnp@titlesc is missing}%
    {Keep the retained title small caps as a private macro.}}{}
% Its old public name must be gone (no compatibility alias).
\@ifundefined{titlesc}{}%
  {\PackageError{title}{Public titlesc must be removed, not aliased}%
    {The v3 contraction removes the generic small-caps API.}}
\makeatother

\begin{document}
\articletitle{A Retained Title Surface}
\articleauthors{Jane Q. Author}
\articledate{August 2026}
\begin{articleabstract}
The retained front matter renders with the private small caps, visually
unchanged by the generic-API contraction.
\end{articleabstract}
\articlekeywords{typography, contraction, coexistence}
\articlejel{C10, D20}

\section{Body}
Body text follows the retained title surface.
\end{document}
